newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat export pace tied to tender bids - Legras.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat export pace tied to tender bids - Legras.

text.p: The European Union, which last week granted an increase in wheat exports, will closely watch the bids at a weekly tender when deciding future exports, Guy Legras, director general for agriculture at the European Commission, said on Monday.
"It is a question of bids," Legras told Reuters by telephone from Brussels, adding that last week's bids based on a marked reduction in refunds had been considered "good".
Refunds fell 3.5 Ecus per tonne from the previous week and the EU was able to award licences for an unusually high 398,500 tonnes of free-market soft wheat, he said.
The EU cut its maximum refund to 12.90 Ecus per tonne from 16.40 Ecus and awarded its highest export volume for a single week since 429,300 tonnes on December 5.
Previously in February, the EU had awarded between 115,000 and 238,000 tonnes of soft wheat at the Thursday tender.
Asked whether Brussels would continue to export around 400,000 tonnes each week, Legras said, "That depends solely on the quality of the bids."
Exporters have been protesting about the level of refund awarded by the Commission, saying it is too low to cover recent grain sales to Mediterranean buyers.
At current prices refunds of 16-17 Ecus per tonne are needed to avoid financial losses, they say.
Exporters last week bid for more than 900,000 tonnes of wheat through France at refunds up to 17.74 Ecus per tonne.
According to some traders the industry is short of licences for up to a million tonnes of wheat.
While focusing mainly on the question of bids, Legras also said internal wheat prices had seemed "a little high" last week.
The Commission has long held a policy of curbing domestic price rises to maintain wheat's competitiveness against other animal feed ingredients, a key target of its 1992 farm reform.
